figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Our framework of Chronos. Given reference images, a raw prompt, and optional temporal captions, the pipeline first performs Semantic Prompt Anchoring, then generates frame anchors through Visual Frame Anchoring, where Track 1 uses a single anchor $A_{1}$, and Track 2 may use additional segment-level anchors $\{A_{t}\}_{t=2}^{T}$. The enhanced prompt and anchors are passed to track-specific video generators, followed by metric-guided evaluation and automatic routing to obtain the final video.A left-to-right four-stage flowchart. Reference images, a raw prompt, and optional temporal captions enter Semantic Prompt Anchoring, which extracts identity cues and applies one of three levels of risk-aware prompt adaptation. Visual Frame Anchoring then uses the enhanced prompt and temporal captions to create one or more ordered frame anchors. Multiple video generators produce candidate videos, which are scored for text consistency, subject preservation, video quality, and an LLM-based assessment before exception-aware review selects the final video.

abstract: Identity-preserving video generation aims to synthesize high-quality and visually realistic videos from textual and visual conditions while faithfully maintaining the subject’s identity across diverse motions. Prior methods have extensively introduced reference-guided control signals and identity-aware conditioning to improve facial alignment from reference images. However, improving static identity alignment alone creates a fundamental tension between identity fidelity and temporal controllability, which frequently causes identity drift or motion suppression under large pose variations and multi-segment sequential actions. To address this, we propose Chronos, a framework that unifies single-segment facial identity preservation and multi-segment sequential action generation under a common temporal formulation. Specifically, Chronos integrates Semantic Prompt Anchoring to adaptively refine the user prompt, Visual Frame Anchoring to transform conditions into visually grounded keyframe anchors for visual guidance, and Metric-Guided Candidate Routing to select the highest-quality videos from heterogeneous generators via multi-dimensional evaluation. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the superiority of our approach, which achieved first place in both Track 1 and Track 2 of the ACM MM 2026 Identity-Preserving Video Generation Challenge, demonstrating its effectiveness across both facial identity preservation and sequential action generation settings.

sections.body: Identity-preserving video generation faces a tension: strong identity constraints can suppress motion, while weak ones cause identity drift under large poses, occlusions, and multi-segment actions. Chronos addresses this with three stages. Semantic Prompt Anchoring extracts identity cues from reference images and refines the prompt. Visual Frame Anchoring produces a first-frame anchor or cascaded keyframe anchors using an image-to-image operator. Metric-Guided Candidate Routing generates candidates from several video generators, scores them across several dimensions, and selects the highest-scoring video. The paper reports first place in Track 1 and Track 2 of the ACM MM 2026 Identity-Preserving Video Generation Challenge. Quantitative comparisons appear in later sections.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Chronos is a training-free framework that unifies single-segment identity preservation with multi-segment sequential action generation.

sections.body: The section groups prior work on identity-preserving generation. ID-Animator uses a face adapter, ConsistID uses frequency-domain facial features, and PersonalVideo jointly models identity and semantic consistency. MagicID targets enhanced motion dynamics, while Phantom, VACE, Stand-In and RefAlign use reference-guided control. For multi-subject work, Kaleido introduces R-RoPE for background disentanglement, and ID-Crafter reports competitive multi-subject results. The authors state that existing approaches still face challenges in keeping temporal consistency while preserving subject identities. Their keyframe-guided framework fuses multi-reference information into identity-aware starting frames and uses first-last-frame generation for transitions between segments.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior identity-preserving methods often trade identity fidelity against motion, and multi-subject methods still struggle with temporal consistency.

sections.body: Track 1 is the single-segment case with T=1 and Track 2 is the multi-segment case with T>1. Semantic Prompt Anchoring uses a GPT model to extract an identity representation from the reference images, discarding clothing and background, then assigns a risk-aware augmentation score from {1,2,3} and adds viewpoint and visibility cues. Visual Frame Anchoring creates a first-frame anchor for Track 1. For Track 2 it builds anchors in a cascade, reusing earlier keyframes as visual conditions. Metric-Guided Candidate Routing scores candidates on text, identity, subject, motion, quality and LLM-based dimensions. The selected output maximizes $R(V_{k})=\sum_{j}\lambda_{j}s_{j}(V_{k})$, and any output with a critical score below its threshold goes to human review. The section gives no values for the weights or thresholds.
sections.heading: Methodology
sections.headline: Chronos selects the top-scoring candidate from several generators and sends critical-failure outputs to human review.

sections.body: Table 3 ablates the modules against a baseline on both tracks. Adding SPA raises the Track 1 Subject Score from 0.7511 to 0.7557. The full Chronos model reaches a Track 1 Total Score of 0.6833, up from a baseline of 0.6353, and a Track 2 Total Score of 0.6530, up from 0.5803. The text reports approximately 9.0% higher Total Score than the runner-up RefAlign on Track 1 and 6.6% over Phantom on Track 2. It also notes that RefAlign yields higher facial similarity. The ablation uses the first 100 cases because of evaluation cost, and its baseline is VACE.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: Adding all components raises Total Score over the baseline on both tracks, from 0.6353 to 0.6833 and 0.5803 to 0.6530.

sections.body: The conclusion restates the framework. Identity cues from reference images adjust prompt visibility and viewpoint cues, cascaded keyframe anchors ground the action phases, and multi-dimensional evaluation selects outputs from several generators with an exception-aware filter. It reports first place in Track 1 and Track 2 of the ACM MM 2026 Identity-Preserving Video Generation Challenge. The section adds no new measurements beyond those in the experiments.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Chronos is summarized as a training-free framework whose selection step produced first place on both challenge tracks.
